events.pleaseNote: Richard Thomas in Mark Twain Tonight by Hal Holbrook Emmy-Award® winning Actor and 2025 Theater Hall of Fame Inductee Richard Thomas brings to life "the nation's one true comic genius" (The New York Times) in Mark Twain Tonight!, written and originally performed by Hal Holbrook. Join the millions who have cheered for the legendary one-man show, bursting with Twain's "uproariously funny" and "pungently wise" (Time Magazine) humor. Most recently seen on Broadway in Our Town, on tour as Atticus Finch in To Kill a Mockingbird, and on Netflix's Ozark, Richard Thomas will return to Broadway in Spring 2026 in David Lindsay-Abaire's The Balusters, directed by Kenny Leon. Beloved to generations as John-Boy Walton, Richard Thomas is the first and only actor authorized to perform Mark Twain Tonight! since the original.

events.pleaseNote: The Boise State University Symphony Orchestra celebrates the powerful connections between music, place, and home in " 'Suite' and Lasting Impressions of Home." From the sweeping patriotism of Sibelius' Finlandia and the vivid Norwegian landscapes of Grieg's Peer Gynt to the folk traditions of Smetana, Vaughan Williams, and Copland, the program explores the many ways composers have drawn inspiration from the countries, cultures, and traditions closest to them. The concert will also feature one of our 2027 Concerto-Aria Competition winners and culminates with Arturo Márquez's exhilarating Danzón No. 2, a vibrant celebration of Mexican dance and rhythm. Boise State University Students, Staff and Faculty are eligible for one complimentary ticket - please visit the Morrison Center Ticket Office with valid ID in ADVANCE of performance.

events.pleaseNote: Experience the power and artistry of the Boise State Symphonic Winds, a nationally recognized ensemble of dedicated student musicians performing cornerstone repertoire alongside compelling contemporary works. Led by Dr. Myron Peterson, the ensemble aims to connect people through music, offering programs that challenge audiences to contemplate their relationship with various universal and human themes. Featuring the finest woodwind, brass, and percussion artists on campus, this premier wind band delivers engaging professional performances showcasing technical precision and vivid expression. Symphonic Winds is pleased to share this concert with the Boise State All-Star High School Honor Band under the direction of guest artist Dr. John Lynch. Boise State University Students, Staff and Faculty are eligible for one complimentary ticket - please visit the Morrison Center Ticket Office with valid ID in ADVANCE of performance.

events.pleaseNote: Collision of Rhythm is a duo comprised of tap-dancing classical virtuoso, Aaron Williams, and beatbox-juggling keynote speaker, Bronkar Lee. They have worked with companies like GoPro, Coca Cola, and Google, and have been featured on The Tonight Show, America's Got Talent, and SuperBowl commercials. Both have achieved internet fame with "rhythmic" viral videos - Aaron, through his virtuosic rendition of Mario on Marimba (over 100 million views), and Bronkar, as the Beatbox Dad, through a video of him beatboxing with his son (over 200 million views). Season tickets are available!

accessibility.info:
Up to (3) companions per accessible patron.  Please make every attempt to limit the number of companions in adjacent seating to (1). Place other companions (as possible) in the row just behind the wheelchair space(s). 

Wheelchair seating in Main Hall is available in Row I and (K for extra companion seating) of the Orchestra Level, and Row E and (G for extra companion seating) of the Mezzanine Level. See seating chart for details. Accessible locations are reserved for use by patrons with disabilities, but may be released for general sale when all other locations are sold. If you are planning on transferring to a theater seat from a wheelchair or mobility device, please inform the ticket office when ordering so we may seat you in an appropriate and safe location. Fire safety codes forbid items such as wheelchairs and mobility devices from being left in any aisle where they may become an obstruction in an emergency.

boxOfficeInfo.willCallDetail: Will Call is available 90 minutes prior to showtime and is located at the Morrison Center Box Office unless otherwise indicated.

venues.parkingDetail: Parking for ticket purchases is available in the 15 minute loading zone in front of the Box Office located on W Friendship Ln (river/North side of the Morrison Center). Event parking is available in the Brady Garage at University and Earle St and nearby surface lots. Those needing accessible parking will be directed to a limited number of spaces near the Morrison Center academic entrance or the first floor of the Brady Garage. Attendants will be on hand to offer directions and assistance. Patrons are strongly encouraged to plan ahead and arrive at least 30 minutes prior to show time. Event parking is included in the price of all Morrison Center Main Hall performances.
venues.accessibleSeatingDetail: Accessible seating locations are shown on the event interactive seat map. For more information please visit www.MorrisonCenter.com or call 208.426.1111. Wheelchair seating in Main Hall is available in Row I and (K for extra companion seating) of the Orchestra Level, and Row E and (G for extra companion seating) of the Mezzanine Level. See seating chart for details. Accessible locations are reserved for use by patrons with disabilities, but may be released for general sale when all other locations are sold. If you are planning on transferring to a theater seat from a wheelchair or mobility device, please inform the ticket office when ordering so we may seat you in an appropriate and safe location. Fire safety codes forbid items such as wheelchairs and mobility devices from being left in any aisle where they may become an obstruction in an emergency. Only entries 1, 11 & 12 completely avoid stair steps on approach from lobby. Up to (4) companions per accessible patron. Please make every attempt to limit the number of companions in adjacent seating to (1). Place other companions (as possible) in the row just behind the wheelchair space(s). For information regarding Mobility/Sight/Hearing Impairment accommodations, please purchase seats designated as wheelchair accessible or call (208) 426-1111. Sign Language Interpretation for Morrison Center sponsored performances requires a minimum of 72 hrs. prior notice. Please call the Special Assistance Line at (208) 426-1111 Monday-Friday 10AM-3PM well in advance to schedule an interpreter. Assistive listening headsets are available at all Morrison Center sponsored performances and may be picked up at the information booth in the main lobby.
